title: The Wild World of Money in College Football

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Natalie Kittroweff, in for Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是娜塔莉·基特罗夫，代班萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西。

sentences.en: Tonight, millions of Americans will tune in to watch one of the biggest sports events of the year, college football's national championship game.
sentences.zh: 今晚，数百万美国人将收看年度最大的体育赛事之一：大学橄榄球全国冠军赛。

sentences.en: On the field, the game will be determined by the skill of the players and coaches.
sentences.zh: 在赛场上，比赛胜负将由球员和教练的水平决定。

sentences.en: But behind the scenes, secretive groups of donors are wielding enormous influence over what fans will see.
sentences.zh: 但在幕后，神秘的捐赠者群体正在对球迷所看到的一切施加巨大的影响。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague David Farenthold on the shadowy industry upending college football and how it's brought amateur athletics even closer to the world of professional sports.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事大卫·法伦索尔德将带我们了解那个正在颠覆大学橄榄球的阴影产业，以及它如何让业余体育运动与职业体育世界靠得更近。

sentences.en: It's Monday, January 8th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月8日，星期一。

sentences.en: David, hi.
sentences.zh: 大卫，你好。

sentences.en: Hi, Natalie.
sentences.zh: 你好，娜塔莉。

sentences.en: It's nice to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: So, you're an investigative reporter at the New York Times, and recently you've been looking into the world of college sports.
sentences.zh: 你是《纽约时报》的一名调查记者，最近你一直在关注大学体育界。

sentences.en: Tell me why.
sentences.zh: 告诉我为什么。

sentences.en: Well, college sports is, to me, a fascinating subject because there's so much money involved here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对我来说，大学体育是一个引人入胜的话题，因为这里面涉及的资金太庞大了。

sentences.en: I think people have this sense that college sports is amateur athletics, but the amounts of money brought in to these college football programs, particularly,
sentences.zh: 我认为人们有一种观念，觉得大学体育是业余运动，但这些大学橄榄球项目所带来的资金，尤其是，

sentences.en: are in the billions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 是以十亿美元计的。

sentences.en: I'm an investigative reporter covering nonprofits.
sentences.zh: 我是一名报道非营利组织的调查记者。

sentences.en: Obviously, colleges are nonprofits, so it's one of the biggest businesses that nonprofits carry out.
sentences.zh: 显然，大学本身就是非营利组织，所以这是非营利组织所经营的最大业务之一。

sentences.en: And there's also a personal connection for me.
sentences.zh: 而且对我个人来说，也有某种联系。

sentences.en: I'm a huge college sports fan, and the team I follow is the University of Texas Longhorns.
sentences.zh: 我是大学体育的超级粉丝，我支持的球队是德克萨斯大学长角牛队。

sentences.en: I've been a fan of UT since I was a little kid.
sentences.zh: 我从小就是长角牛队的粉丝。

sentences.en: So, the way I got into this story was late 2021, I saw a press release from a group at the University of Texas supporting Longhorns, and it was a charity.
sentences.zh: 我接触到这个故事是在2021年底，我看到德克萨斯大学一个支持长角牛队的组织发布了一份新闻稿，那是一个慈善机构。

sentences.en: It was a nonprofit, the topic that I had just gotten interested in writing about.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非营利组织，正是我刚开始感兴趣报道的主题。

sentences.en: And this charity was doing something really odd, something I'd never seen before.
sentences.zh: 这个慈善机构在做一件非常奇怪的事情，我以前从未见过。

sentences.en: They were saying, the reason our charity exists is to pay offensive linemen at the University of Texas, to pay football players.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们慈善机构存在的理由就是为了给德克萨斯大学的进攻锋线球员发钱，给橄榄球运动员发钱。

sentences.en: Particularly, they were saying, we're going to pay every offensive lineman on the University of Texas team $50,000 a year.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，他们说，我们要给德克萨斯大学队的每一位进攻锋线球员每年5万美元。

sentences.en: And all you have to do to get the money is to be on the team, to be academically eligible to play.
sentences.zh: 而你所要做的就是成为球队的一员，并且在学业上符合参赛资格。

sentences.en: Now, that struck me, I mean, as a UT fan, great, I'm glad, whatever it takes to get better offensive linemen.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到震惊，我的意思是，作为长角牛队的粉丝，这很好，我很高兴，无论付出什么代价能让进攻锋线变得更强都行。

sentences.en: But as a nonprofit reporter, that struck me really strangely, because, you know, that's not what charities do.
sentences.zh: 但作为一名报道非营利组织的记者，这让我觉得非常奇怪，因为你知道，慈善机构不是这么运作的。

sentences.en: Charities don't pay offensive linemen.
sentences.zh: 慈善机构不会给进攻锋线球员发工资。

sentences.en: And I was struggling to figure out how they're squaring their mission of helping the public good with their apparent goal of helping the University of Texas win football games.
sentences.zh: 我一直在努力弄清楚，他们是如何将“造福公众”的使命与他们“帮助德克萨斯大学赢得橄榄球比赛”的明显目标协调起来的。

sentences.en: So I started looking into this, and what I found was that this University of Texas group was one of more than 100 groups
sentences.zh: 所以我开始调查这件事，我发现德克萨斯大学的这个组织只是全国100多个组织中的一个，

sentences.en: that were doing similar things at schools all around the country, using cash from donors to pay athletes
sentences.zh: 它们在全国各地的学校做着类似的事情，利用捐赠者的现金来支付运动员，

sentences.en: and to attract athletes to their school to keep them when they were already there.
sentences.zh: 并吸引运动员到他们的学校，或者在他们已经在校时留住他们。

sentences.en: And what I also found was that those payments were kind of, in a way that maybe not be obvious to the average fan,
sentences.zh: 我还发现，这些支付方式在某种程度上，可能对普通球迷来说并不明显，

sentences.en: and definitely not obvious to the casual fan, were reshaping the power dynamics, the rules, the very sort of essence of big-time college football.
sentences.zh: 对休闲球迷来说绝对不明显，它们正在重塑顶级大学橄榄球的权力动态、规则，甚至是其本质。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: Tell me more about that.
sentences.zh: 多跟我说说这个。

sentences.en: Well, we all know that college sports is an amateur game.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们都知道大学体育是一项业余运动。

sentences.en: You can't be paid for playing the game.
sentences.zh: 你不能因为参加比赛而获得报酬。

sentences.en: That was the hallmark of college sports for decades, and it was strictly policed by the NCAA, the organization that sort of oversees big-time college sports.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，这一直是大学体育的标志，并受到NCAA（监管顶级大学体育的组织）的严格监管。

sentences.en: The consequences for paying players under the table could be very high.
sentences.zh: 私下给球员发钱的后果可能非常严重。

sentences.en: Southern Methodist University famously got what they called the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 南卫理公会大学就曾因所谓的“死刑”处罚而闻名。

sentences.en: Their football team was shut down for a year because their boosters were paying players back in the 80s, and it took them 30 years to recover.
sentences.zh: 他们的橄榄球队被停赛了一年，因为他们的支持者在80年代给球员发钱，他们花了30年才恢复元气。

sentences.en: So officially, even though many of these schools were benefiting financially from college sports,
sentences.zh: 所以从官方层面来看，尽管许多学校从大学体育中获得了经济利益，

sentences.en: there was this red line that none of that money was supposed to go to student-athletes.
sentences.zh: 但有一条红线，即这些钱都不应该流向学生运动员。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Hundreds of millions of dollars, billions of dollars, flowing into these schools collectively from TV deals, from ticket sales, and it finds all these other channels.
sentences.zh: 数以亿计、数十亿美元的资金通过电视转播协议、门票销售集体流入这些学校，并流向了其他所有渠道。

sentences.en: Coaches get paid tens of millions of dollars a year, and the money would get filtered to players in a way in that they would get scholarships,
sentences.zh: 教练们每年拿着数千万美元的薪水，而钱会以奖学金的形式过滤给球员，

sentences.en: and they would get a nice dorm to live in, very nice athletic facilities.
sentences.zh: 他们会得到不错的宿舍住，还有非常好的运动设施。

sentences.en: But the players did not get paid, and that was both the rule and also sort of the moral heart of college sports for so long, was this is an amateur game.
sentences.zh: 但球员们没有拿到工资，这在很长一段时间里既是规则，也是大学体育的道德核心，即这是一项业余运动。

sentences.en: But then in 2021...
sentences.zh: 但到了2021年……

sentences.en: It's being called a game-changer for college athletes who...
sentences.zh: 这被称为大学运动员的游戏规则改变者，他们……

sentences.en: That system changed drastically.
sentences.zh: 那个系统发生了剧变。

sentences.en: You're going to have quarterbacks and point guards and pitchers making thousands, if not hundreds of thousands, if not millions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 你将会看到四分卫、控球后卫和投手赚取数千，甚至数十万，甚至数百万美元。

sentences.en: Now, this was a change that the NCAA didn't want.
sentences.zh: 现在，这是NCAA不想要的改变。

sentences.en: It was forced on the NCAA, in part by state legislatures.
sentences.zh: 这是在州立法机构的部分推动下强加给NCAA的。

sentences.en: Student-athletes in Missouri are one signature away from making a profit off their name and likeness.
sentences.zh: 密苏里州的学生运动员距离从他们的姓名和肖像权中获利只差一个签名。

sentences.en: Which had started to pass laws saying that athletes in their state should be able to make endorsements to get paid.
sentences.zh: 各州开始通过法律，规定本州的运动员应该能够通过代言获得报酬。

sentences.en: Today, the Supreme Court will hear arguments on whether the NCAA has the authority...
sentences.zh: 今天，最高法院将听取关于NCAA是否有权……的辩论。

sentences.en: There was also a Supreme Court case...
sentences.zh: 还有一个最高法院的案件……

sentences.en: The schools are conspiring to pay no salaries to the workers who are making the schools billions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 学校正在合谋不给那些为学校创造数十亿美元收入的劳动者支付工资。

sentences.en: In which the justices ruled unanimously against the NCAA, against its ability to control what athletes receive as compensation.
sentences.zh: 大法官们一致裁定反对NCAA，反对其控制运动员获得补偿的能力。

sentences.en: Name, image, and likeness.
sentences.zh: 姓名、形象和肖像权。

sentences.en: It's revolutionizing college sports.
sentences.zh: 它正在彻底改变大学体育。

sentences.en: The result was something called the NIL, name, image, and likeness, rules, which the NCAA put in place, again, under duress, in the summer of 2021.
sentences.zh: 结果就是所谓的NIL（姓名、形象和肖像权）规则，NCAA在2021年夏天再次被迫实施了这些规则。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This was a huge deal at the time.
sentences.zh: 这在当时是一件大事。

sentences.en: And if I remember correctly, the expectation was that the players, the students, would be able to make money from brand sponsorships and things like that, capitalize on their fame.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，当时的预期是球员、学生们能够通过品牌赞助等方式赚钱，利用他们的名气获利。

sentences.en: But they couldn't be treated like employees who were making a salary.
sentences.zh: 但他们不能被当作拿工资的雇员来对待。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That was very, very important to the NCAA.
sentences.zh: 这对NCAA来说非常、非常重要。

sentences.en: Both because the schools don't want to part with any of the huge amount of money they were making off college sports,
sentences.zh: 这不仅是因为学校不想放弃他们从大学体育中赚取的巨额资金，

sentences.en: but also because if you treat them as employees, there's a whole bunch of other things that cascade from that.
sentences.zh: 还因为如果你把他们当作雇员，就会引发一系列连锁反应。

sentences.en: The control that universities have over players in this current system, where they're just student-athletes and not employees,
sentences.zh: 在目前的体系下，大学对球员的控制权——他们只是学生运动员而不是雇员——

sentences.en: would be eroded if they were basically professional athletes.
sentences.zh: 如果他们本质上是职业运动员，这种控制权就会被削弱。

sentences.en: Think how much more rights and power a professional football player has than a college football player has.
sentences.zh: 想想看，职业橄榄球运动员比大学橄榄球运动员拥有多少更多的权利和权力。

sentences.en: The NCAA did not want to usher in that system.
sentences.zh: NCAA不想引入那样的体系。

sentences.en: So, David, were there rules around this sponsorship money?
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫，关于这些赞助费有什么规则吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: Most importantly, there was a rule that said nothing about the payments anybody makes to players can be conditioned on them playing at all or on them playing well.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，有一条规则规定，任何人支付给球员的钱，都不能以他们是否参赛或表现好坏为条件。

sentences.en: And the second thing was you can't use these payments, these NIL payments,
sentences.zh: 第二点是，你不能利用这些支付，这些NIL支付，

sentences.en: to recruit players, either to recruit high schoolers or to recruit people from other schools to your school.
sentences.zh: 来招募球员，无论是招募高中生还是从其他学校挖人到你的学校。

sentences.en: Those were the guidelines the NCAA set.
sentences.zh: 这就是NCAA设定的指导方针。

sentences.en: But almost immediately after these rules come into effect, wealthy boosters, rich folks who support these teams, see a loophole.
sentences.zh: 但这些规则生效后几乎立即，富有的支持者，那些支持这些球队的富人，就看到了漏洞。

sentences.en: They see an opening for themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们为自己看到了机会。

sentences.en: They start these things called collectives, which are groups that are not legally affiliated with the schools they support,
sentences.zh: 他们开始组建所谓的“集体”（collectives），这些组织在法律上并不隶属于他们所支持的学校，

sentences.en: but they exist to support a specific school's athletic prograMs.
sentences.zh: 但它们的存在是为了支持特定学校的体育项目。

sentences.en: And what they do is pool money from rich donors, and it can be millions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 他们所做的是从富有的捐赠者那里筹集资金，金额可能高达数百万美元。

sentences.en: And they pay athletes for the rights to their name, in some cases for the athletes to do charity work,
sentences.zh: 他们为运动员的姓名权付费，在某些情况下是为了让运动员做慈善工作，

sentences.en: make an appearance at the Boys and Girls Club, to appear at another charity's gala, to post about charity on social media.
sentences.zh: 比如在男孩女孩俱乐部露面，在其他慈善机构的晚会上露面，或者在社交媒体上发布关于慈善的内容。

sentences.en: But often these charities pay way more than an actual charity would pay for this.
sentences.zh: 但通常这些慈善机构为此支付的费用远高于实际慈善机构的水平。

sentences.en: I talked to somebody who was at Michigan State, and he paid somebody $750,000 a year, a football player,
sentences.zh: 我采访过一个在密歇根州立大学的人，他每年付给一个人75万美元，一个橄榄球运动员，

sentences.en: and the charity work that person did in return was to make one social media post a month.
sentences.zh: 而那个人作为回报所做的慈善工作就是每个月发一条社交媒体帖子。

sentences.en: Well, they're paying athletes often who don't have much of an endorsement value, people who are really valuable to their own team, like an offensive lineman or a fullback.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们支付的运动员往往没有什么代言价值，那些对他们自己的球队真正有价值的人，比如进攻锋线球员或全卫。

sentences.en: They're paying that person according to their value to the team, not according to their endorsement value.
sentences.zh: 他们是根据那个人对球队的价值来支付报酬的，而不是根据他们的代言价值。

sentences.en: So this is not a person you would ever buy Gatorade from.
sentences.zh: 所以这根本不是你会买佳得乐（Gatorade）代言的那种人。

sentences.en: You'd have never heard this person's name, but, you know, the team needs them.
sentences.zh: 你可能从未听说过这个人的名字，但是，你知道，球队需要他们。

sentences.en: And a lot of these groups organize themselves as tax-exempt charities.
sentences.zh: 而且许多这样的组织将自己组织为免税慈善机构。

sentences.en: They get approval from the IRS.
sentences.zh: 他们获得了国税局（IRS）的批准。

sentences.en: So that means that their donations from donors are tax-deductible.
sentences.zh: 这意味着捐赠者的捐款是可以抵税的。

sentences.en: It's a double benefit.
sentences.zh: 这是双重好处。

sentences.en: You could get the linebacker you want, and you get a tax deduction.
sentences.zh: 你既能得到你想要的线卫，又能获得税收减免。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So you have these collectives, these outside groups that are theoretically not attached to the universities, and they are ostensibly paying for charitable work.
sentences.zh: 所以你有这些“集体”，这些理论上不附属于大学的外部组织，它们表面上是在为慈善工作买单。

sentences.en: But really, this is all just a cover for recruitment for these teaMs.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这只是为这些球队招募球员的掩护。

sentences.en: That's the weird thing about this system is that, yes, the things that they are specifically prohibited from doing, paying players to play,
sentences.zh: 这个系统最奇怪的地方在于，是的，那些明确禁止他们做的事情，比如付钱让球员参赛，

sentences.en: you know, coordinating with schools to make sure they get the players the schools want, and recruiting players with money, those three things which you're not allowed to do,
sentences.zh: 你知道，与学校协调以确保他们得到学校想要的球员，以及用钱招募球员，这三件你不被允许做的事情，

sentences.en: those are the reasons you have a collective.
sentences.zh: 正是你拥有一个“集体”的原因。

sentences.en: Those are the things the collective is built to do.
sentences.zh: 这些正是“集体”建立的目的。

sentences.en: Those are the functions of a collective, truly.
sentences.zh: 这确实是“集体”的功能。

sentences.en: So all the things that they're doing, that they're designed to do, that they're gathering money from donors to do, are the things that theoretically they're not allowed to do.
sentences.zh: 所以他们所做的所有事情，他们被设计要做的事情，他们从捐赠者那里筹集资金要做的事情，都是理论上他们不被允许做的事情。

sentences.en: And so you have this weird flowering of a system with a gigantic wink and a nod that is doing for every school what the NCAA says shouldn't happen in any school.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到了一个奇怪的系统在蓬勃发展，大家心照不宣，它正在为每一所学校做着NCAA声称不应该在任何学校发生的事情。

sentences.en: Can you give me an example of how this actually works?
sentences.zh: 你能给我举个例子说明这是怎么运作的吗？

sentences.en: Well, a great example is that University of Texas collective I was talking about,
sentences.zh: 嗯，一个很好的例子就是我刚才提到的德克萨斯大学的那个“集体”，

sentences.en: Horns With Heart.
sentences.zh: “心系长角牛”（Horns With Heart）。

sentences.en: People who are not University of Texas fans like me may not know, but 2021 was a bad year for the Texas Longhorns.
sentences.zh: 像我这样不是德克萨斯大学粉丝的人可能不知道，但2021年对德克萨斯长角牛队来说是糟糕的一年。

sentences.en: They are a proud program.
sentences.zh: 他们是一支自豪的球队。

sentences.en: They've had some great national championships, but they were at a low ebb at that point.
sentences.zh: 他们曾获得过伟大的全国冠军，但在那时处于低谷。

sentences.en: They had a losing season, which, you know, was rare for them.
sentences.zh: 他们经历了一个输球的赛季，你知道，这对他们来说很少见。

sentences.en: They lost six games in a row at one point for the first time since the 50s.
sentences.zh: 他们一度连续输掉了六场比赛，这是自50年代以来的第一次。

sentences.en: The season has ended.
sentences.zh: 赛季结束了。

sentences.en: They're not going to a bowl game.
sentences.zh: 他们没能进入碗赛。

sentences.en: Everybody in Austin is depressed.
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀的每个人都很沮丧。

sentences.en: Things were bad.
sentences.zh: 情况很糟糕。

sentences.en: And the coach has an answer.
sentences.zh: 教练有一个答案。

sentences.en: He says, we need linemen.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们需要锋线球员。

sentences.en: We need the big blockers up front who will give the quarterback time to throw.
sentences.zh: 我们需要前面的大块头阻挡者，他们能给四分卫传球的时间。

sentences.en: We'll give the running back room to run.
sentences.zh: 我们会给跑卫留出奔跑的空间。

sentences.en: We need bigger humans.
sentences.zh: 我们需要更大块头的人。

sentences.en: And so that's when this collective comes in with its promise to pay $50,000 to any lineman who plays at the University of Texas.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是那个“集体”介入的时候，承诺给任何在德克萨斯大学打球的锋线球员支付5万美元。

sentences.en: And it works.
sentences.zh: 而且它奏效了。

sentences.en: I talked recently to a number of linemen who are at the University of Texas now.
sentences.zh: 我最近和一些现在在德克萨斯大学的锋线球员谈过。

sentences.en: One example, this guy, Cameron WilliaMs.
sentences.zh: 一个例子，这个叫卡梅伦·威廉姆斯（Cameron Williams）的家伙。

sentences.en: So he is a 6'5", 370 pounds, huge prospect coming out of high school in Dallas.
sentences.zh: 他身高6英尺5英寸，体重370磅，是达拉斯高中出来的一个巨大的潜力股。

sentences.en: He had committed already to a different school.
sentences.zh: 他已经承诺去另一所学校了。

sentences.en: He committed to Oregon to play for the Oregon Ducks.
sentences.zh: 他承诺去俄勒冈大学为俄勒冈鸭队效力。

sentences.en: This promise comes out.
sentences.zh: 这个承诺一出来。

sentences.en: He decommits from Oregon and commits to University of Texas a week later.
sentences.zh: 他一周后就撤回了对俄勒冈的承诺，转而承诺去德克萨斯大学。

sentences.en: And what he told me was, look, I come from a family without much money.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我的是，看，我来自一个没多少钱的家庭。

sentences.en: You know, this was a chance for me to get $50,000 and help my family right away.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是我获得5万美元并立即帮助家人的机会。

sentences.en: I don't have to wait four years and hope I make the NFL draft.
sentences.zh: 我不必等四年，祈祷自己能进入NFL选秀。

sentences.en: I can help my family right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在就能帮助我的家人。

sentences.en: So why wouldn't I do it?
sentences.zh: 那我为什么不这么做呢？

sentences.en: So that offseason, Texas had wanted five good offensive linemen.
sentences.zh: 所以那个休赛期，德克萨斯大学本来想要五个好的进攻锋线球员。

sentences.en: They got seven with the help of this collective, with the help of this offer, $50,000.
sentences.zh: 在那个“集体”的帮助下，在5万美元报价的帮助下，他们得到了七个。

sentences.en: And it starts a rebuilding program that takes Texas from that really low ebb to where they were this year, which is they had a spot in the college football semifinals.
sentences.zh: 这开启了一个重建计划，让德克萨斯大学从那个非常低的低谷走到了今年的位置，也就是他们获得了大学橄榄球半决赛的一个席位。

sentences.en: They were one of the last four teams standing.
sentences.zh: 他们是最后剩下的四支球队之一。

sentences.en: Now, they lost to Washington at the very end of the great game, but that collective, the promise they made, the linemen they brought in, took them from a pretty low ebb back to
sentences.zh: 虽然他们在最后一场精彩比赛的末尾输给了华盛顿大学，但那个集体、他们做出的承诺、他们引进的锋线球员，把他们从低谷带回到了

sentences.en: almost the top of college football.
sentences.zh: 几乎是大学橄榄球的巅峰。

sentences.en: So that's a sign of the potential these collectives have for even well-established programs like
sentences.zh: 所以，这表明了这些集体对于像

sentences.en: Texas.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯大学这样成熟的项目也具有巨大的潜力。

sentences.en: It's kind of amazing, David, in this example you're giving.
sentences.zh: 大卫，你举的这个例子真是令人惊叹。

sentences.en: You see in real time how this money affects the makeup of college sports.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时看到这些资金如何影响大学体育的构成。

sentences.en: You have a kid openly, you know, switching schools because of the offer.
sentences.zh: 你看到一个孩子因为报价而公开转学。

sentences.en: I mean, you see these collectives at work recruiting players that teams are specifically saying they need to win.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你看到这些集体在招募球员时，球队明确表示他们需要这些球员才能获胜。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, I don't want to be naive.
sentences.zh: 我不想表现得太天真。

sentences.en: Obviously, in the past, there were times when boosters would pay off players maybe to switch schools or maybe to come to their school.
sentences.zh: 显然，过去也曾有过赞助商付钱给球员，让他们转学或加入自己学校的情况。

sentences.en: But there's a difference here.
sentences.zh: 但这里有一个区别。

sentences.en: It's in a press release.
sentences.zh: 这出现在新闻稿里。

sentences.en: This is above the board.
sentences.zh: 这是公开透明的。

sentences.en: And so the potential number of people who could be swayed by this is so much bigger.
sentences.zh: 因此，可能受此影响的人数要多得多。

sentences.en: And so what Texas does sets a model that other people immediately start to follow.
sentences.zh: 所以德克萨斯大学的做法树立了一个榜样，其他人立刻开始效仿。

sentences.en: They look around and say, hey, you know, we need linemen and we got rich donors.
sentences.zh: 他们环顾四周说，嘿，我们需要锋线球员，我们有富有的捐赠者。

sentences.en: Let's put those two together.
sentences.zh: 让我们把这两者结合起来。

sentences.en: So you start to see this proliferation of collectives all over the country.
sentences.zh: 所以你开始看到这种集体在全国范围内激增。

sentences.en: We've now counted more than 140 at all kinds of different schools that start following Texas's model and that they're raising tons of money and offering it to players.
sentences.zh: 我们现在统计了超过140个各种不同学校的集体，它们开始效仿德克萨斯大学的模式，筹集大量资金并提供给球员。

sentences.en: Many of them also copying Texas's model and that they're doing it through a tax-exempt charity.
sentences.zh: 其中许多也复制了德克萨斯大学的模式，即通过免税慈善机构来运作。

sentences.en: And you start to see that bulwark of college sports, amateurism, the idea that players do it because they love to play or they do it because of the academics, not because they're
sentences.zh: 你开始看到大学体育的支柱——业余精神，即球员因为热爱比赛或为了学业而参赛，而不是因为

sentences.en: getting paid.
sentences.zh: 获得报酬的观念。

sentences.en: That starts to crumble almost immediately after the NIL system came into place.
sentences.zh: 在NIL系统实施后，这种观念几乎立即开始瓦解。

sentences.en: How is all of this affecting the players?
sentences.zh: 这一切对球员有什么影响？

sentences.en: I mean, they must be pretty happy about all this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们对此一定很高兴。

sentences.en: Extremely.
sentences.zh: 非常高兴。

sentences.en: Us having NIL now is such a great thing.
sentences.zh: 我们现在有NIL真是太好了。

sentences.en: I mean, it just benefits guys, especially guys that might not do as well on the next level or, you know, have like career injuries because this game, you could be hurt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这让球员受益匪浅，尤其是那些在下一阶段可能表现不佳，或者因为职业伤病而受影响的人，因为这项运动，你随时可能受伤。

sentences.en: Your career could be over at any given time, you know, so it's a blessing for all of us to be in this time where we're able to get paid.
sentences.zh: 你的职业生涯随时可能结束，所以能在我们这个时代获得报酬对我们所有人来说都是一种福气。

sentences.en: When we've talked to players, they're very happy to get, you know, a little tiny piece.
sentences.zh: 当我们采访球员时，他们很高兴能得到一点点报酬。

sentences.en: And let's face it, it is still a little tiny piece of the huge amount of money that their labor generates.
sentences.zh: 面对现实吧，这仍然只是他们劳动所创造的巨额财富中的一小部分。

sentences.en: NIL's really helped me, you know, put me in a position to where I can take care of my family and where I can help out and stretch my hand out when I'm able to.
sentences.zh: NIL确实帮助了我，让我有能力照顾我的家人，并在我力所能及的时候伸出援手。

sentences.en: When we talked to players, we were asking them in the lead up to the semifinal games last week, you know, what did you use this money for?
sentences.zh: 当我们采访球员时，我们在上周半决赛前夕问他们，你把这些钱用在什么地方了？

sentences.en: And the answers we heard were often.
sentences.zh: 我们听到的答案通常是。

sentences.en: Take care of my daughter.
sentences.zh: 照顾我的女儿。

sentences.en: Pay for daycare every week.
sentences.zh: 每周支付托儿费。

sentences.en: Like, be able to buy her the nice things for Christmas, be able to help out when she needs a flight to come see me.
sentences.zh: 比如，能为她买圣诞礼物，在她需要机票来看我时能提供帮助。

sentences.en: You know, I paid for my family to come up and see a game.
sentences.zh: 我付钱让我的家人来看比赛。

sentences.en: I paid my family's bills.
sentences.zh: 我支付了家人的账单。

sentences.en: Me growing up, I really didn't have money.
sentences.zh: 我成长过程中真的没什么钱。

sentences.en: So, like, the $50,000, it was just, like, amazing.
sentences.zh: 所以，那5万美元简直太惊人了。

sentences.en: It's just, like, shocking me.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: Cameron Williams, University of Texas lineman that came to Texas after seeing that offer of $50,000, she says...
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯大学的锋线球员卡梅伦·威廉姆斯在看到5万美元的报价后加入了德克萨斯大学，她说……

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: So, these players were often thrilled to be able to provide something for their families that they wouldn't have unless they'd gone pro.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些球员通常很高兴能为家人提供一些他们如果不转职业就无法提供的东西。

sentences.en: And, you know, for a lot of these guys, even the good ones, that's still an if and not a when.
sentences.zh: 而且，对于他们中的许多人来说，即使是优秀的球员，那也只是“如果”而不是“何时”。

sentences.en: So, it sounds like the schools are obviously benefiting from this system.
sentences.zh: 所以，听起来学校显然从这个系统中受益。

sentences.en: The donors are also benefiting because they can take credit for rebuilding their team of choice.
sentences.zh: 捐赠者也受益，因为他们可以因重建自己选择的球队而获得功劳。

sentences.en: And the players are, too.
sentences.zh: 球员们也是如此。

sentences.en: Everyone is kind of winning.
sentences.zh: 每个人似乎都是赢家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: On the surface, it does sound like a lot of people are benefiting.
sentences.zh: 从表面上看，确实听起来很多人都受益了。

sentences.en: But you have to remember, what we're talking about here is basically an unregulated black market for labor.
sentences.zh: 但你必须记住，我们在这里讨论的基本上是一个不受监管的劳动力黑市。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of downsides that come with that, including that the system may be unsustainable and parts of it may be illegal.
sentences.zh: 这伴随着很多负面影响，包括这个系统可能是不可持续的，而且部分内容可能是非法的。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟中最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 庆祝175年来帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，获取nytimes.com/subscribe的特别优惠。

sentences.en: David, you've walked us through how these collectives have sort of supercharged paying players in college sports.
sentences.zh: 大卫，你带我们了解了这些集体是如何在大学体育中以某种方式加速支付球员报酬的。

sentences.en: But even though players are getting windfalls of, in some cases, life-changing amounts of money, there are also downsides.
sentences.zh: 但尽管球员们在某些情况下获得了改变生活的意外之财，但也存在负面影响。

sentences.en: Tell me about them.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说这些吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, the players are just really exposed because, as I said, they're basically in an unregulated black market.
sentences.zh: 是的，球员们真的非常脆弱，因为正如我所说，他们基本上处于一个不受监管的劳动力黑市中。

sentences.en: They're getting paid by people who are not really their employers for doing a job that's not really the job they're doing.
sentences.zh: 他们从并非真正雇主的人那里获得报酬，从事的工作也并非他们真正的工作。

sentences.en: There's not that many protections if they get injured.
sentences.zh: 如果他们受伤，几乎没有什么保障。

sentences.en: The collective could stop paying them.
sentences.zh: 集体可能会停止支付他们报酬。

sentences.en: In some cases, collectives have made promises to players, signed contracts, and then not fulfilled them.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，集体曾向球员做出承诺，签署合同，然后却没有履行。

sentences.en: There's a famous example of a player from high school committed to the University of Florida after its collective promised to pay him more than $10 million.
sentences.zh: 有一个著名的例子，一名高中球员在佛罗里达大学的集体承诺支付他超过1000万美元后承诺加入该校。

sentences.en: Then the collective didn't have the money, shut down, and he didn't get paid at all.
sentences.zh: 然后集体没钱了，倒闭了，他一分钱也没拿到。

sentences.en: He transferred to another school.
sentences.zh: 他转学到了另一所学校。

sentences.en: So there's no recourse to rely on if these collectives leave you high and dry.
sentences.zh: 所以如果这些集体让你陷入困境，你没有任何追索权。

sentences.en: So players are really exposed in that way.
sentences.zh: 所以球员在这一方面真的很脆弱。

sentences.en: The second way is that there's just no transparency here.
sentences.zh: 第二个方面是这里根本没有透明度。

sentences.en: There's no way for players to gather the information they need to know how much they should expect to be paid and how much they're worth.
sentences.zh: 球员无法收集他们需要的信息，不知道他们应该期望获得多少报酬以及他们的价值是多少。

sentences.en: Think about professional leagues, right?
sentences.zh: 想想职业联盟，对吧？

sentences.en: We know how much a good second baseman in Major League Baseball ought to get.
sentences.zh: 我们知道美国职业棒球大联盟中一名优秀的二垒手应该得到多少报酬。

sentences.en: We know how much a good quarterback in the National Football League ought to get because there are unions, there's a minimum contract, but there's also a lot of transparency about
sentences.zh: 我们知道国家橄榄球联盟中一名优秀的四分卫应该得到多少报酬，因为有工会，有最低合同，而且对于

sentences.en: what other players at those skill levels and those positions are paid.
sentences.zh: 其他处于相同技能水平和位置的球员的薪水也有很高的透明度。

sentences.en: There's none of that here.
sentences.zh: 这里完全没有这些。

sentences.en: It's all sort of rumors and misinformation.
sentences.zh: 一切都是谣言和错误信息。

sentences.en: So if you're a player or a player in his family trying to navigate this market and find out really what you're worth, it's almost impossible.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是一名球员或球员的家人，试图在这个市场中摸索并找出你真正的价值，这几乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: And the secrecy goes so far that even within teams, we talked to a collective at SMU, Southern
sentences.zh: 而且保密程度之高，甚至在球队内部也是如此，我们采访了南卫理公会大学的一个集体，

sentences.en: Methodist, who said, we tell our players don't ask each other what we're paying you because we don't want you to find out that the guy next to you is getting paid more.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们告诉球员不要互相询问我们付给你们多少钱，因为我们不想让你们发现身边的人拿的钱更多。

sentences.en: And when I say there's no transparency, I've tried that.
sentences.zh: 当我提到没有透明度时，我尝试过。

sentences.en: I sent public records requests to more than 40 public universities about what their NIO collectives are paying their students.
sentences.zh: 我向40多所公立大学发送了公共记录请求，询问他们的NIL集体支付给学生多少钱。

sentences.en: And almost all of them said either that they didn't know or they wouldn't tell us.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有学校都说他们要么不知道，要么不会告诉我们。

sentences.en: In some cases, they wouldn't tell us because basically the logic was we want our football team to win.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，他们不告诉我们是因为逻辑基本上是：我们希望我们的橄榄球队获胜。

sentences.en: And if we tell you what our players get paid, that might result in a collective disadvantage for us.
sentences.zh: 如果我们告诉你球员拿多少钱，那可能会导致我们处于集体劣势。

sentences.en: And so we're just not going to tell you.
sentences.zh: 所以我们就是不告诉你。

sentences.en: That's how hard it is to figure out what the rules are and the standards are in this market.
sentences.zh: 这就是弄清楚这个市场的规则和标准有多难。

sentences.en: I mean, that is a truly extreme level of secrecy that these collectives are treating what are ostensibly charity payments in some cases as a trade secret.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这确实是一种极端的保密程度，这些集体将表面上在某些情况下属于慈善捐款的资金视为商业机密。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And if you pull back, there's a really big equity problem.
sentences.zh: 如果你退一步看，这里有一个非常大的公平问题。

sentences.en: Now, college sports are subject to something called Title IX, which is federal legislation that mandates equal opportunity for female athletes and male athletes.
sentences.zh: 现在，大学体育受到《第九条修正案》的约束，这是一项联邦立法，要求为女性运动员和男性运动员提供平等机会。

sentences.en: Obviously, the decades that Title IX has been in place, it has caused a revolution in women's sports, not just in the college level, but at the professional level.
sentences.zh: 显然，《第九条修正案》实施的几十年里，它不仅在大学层面，而且在职业层面引发了女子体育的革命。

sentences.en: Collectives are, because they're third parties, they're not part of the university, they are not subject to Title IX, and they do not follow it, definitely.
sentences.zh: 集体因为是第三方，不是大学的一部分，所以不受《第九条修正案》的约束，而且他们绝对不遵守它。

sentences.en: So I think the average salary for men's basketball players from collectives is like $30,000 something.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为集体支付给男子篮球运动员的平均工资大约是3万多美元。

sentences.en: The average salary for women's basketball players is like $9,000.
sentences.zh: 女子篮球运动员的平均工资大约是9000美元。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So there's a huge imbalance toward male athletes.
sentences.zh: 所以对男性运动员存在巨大的不平衡。

sentences.en: And the collectives say, you know, that's what our donors want.
sentences.zh: 而集体说，你知道，那是我们捐赠者想要的。

sentences.en: Our donors are, you know, people who like to watch football.
sentences.zh: 我们的捐赠者是喜欢看橄榄球的人。

sentences.en: So, you know, there's no requirement that they share the wealth with, you know, the rest
sentences.zh: 所以，没有要求他们像通过大学获得的资金那样，与学校的其他

sentences.en: of the sports teams at the school the way there is for money that comes through the university.
sentences.zh: 体育团队分享财富。

sentences.en: The other big downside is that a lot of what these groups are doing may be illegal.
sentences.zh: 另一个巨大的负面影响是，这些组织所做的很多事情可能是非法的。

sentences.en: And that goes back to the fact that a lot of them, like the one at University of Texas, are operating as tax-exempt charities.
sentences.zh: 这回到了这样一个事实：他们中的许多人，比如德克萨斯大学的那个，都是作为免税慈善机构运作的。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 解释一下。

sentences.en: We talked before about sort of the rules that tax-exempt charities have to follow.
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈到了免税慈善机构必须遵守的规则。

sentences.en: You know, money in a tax-exempt charity is supposed to be used for the public good, and it can't be used to benefit the private interests of a few people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，免税慈善机构的钱应该用于公共利益，不能用于造福少数人的私人利益。

sentences.en: Now, the IRS is effectively the regulator of nonprofits in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 现在，美国国税局实际上是美国非营利组织的监管机构。

sentences.en: And it allowed a lot of these nonprofits in.
sentences.zh: 它允许很多这样的非营利组织进入。

sentences.en: It gave them tax-exempt status, these collectives.
sentences.zh: 它给了这些集体免税地位。

sentences.en: And then in May of this year, it seemed to reverse itself.
sentences.zh: 然后在今年5月，它似乎推翻了自己的决定。

sentences.en: What the IRS did was put out a memo saying the way that a lot of these collectives operate shows that what they really care about is helping the athletes and helping the team win,
sentences.zh: 国税局发布了一份备忘录，称许多集体运作的方式表明他们真正关心的是帮助运动员和帮助球队获胜，

sentences.en: not helping the public good.
sentences.zh: 而不是帮助公共利益。

sentences.en: And if that's the case, you can't really be a charity.
sentences.zh: 如果情况确实如此，你就不能真正成为慈善机构。

sentences.en: You know, you're not really tax-exempt if that's the case.
sentences.zh: 如果情况如此，你就不是真正的免税。

sentences.en: So it was a warning to all the collectives out there.
sentences.zh: 所以这对所有的集体都是一个警告。

sentences.en: Look, you've got to change in the future.
sentences.zh: 看，未来你们必须改变。

sentences.en: You have to reorganize your operations so that you really are helping the public good first and paying the athletes second.
sentences.zh: 你们必须重组业务，以便真正优先帮助公共利益，其次才是支付运动员报酬。

sentences.en: So a lot of the collectives are sort of grappling with that.
sentences.zh: 所以很多集体都在努力应对这个问题。

sentences.en: Do we just keep doing what we're doing until the IRS comes to us specifically and makes us stop?
sentences.zh: 我们是继续做我们正在做的事情，直到国税局专门找上门来让我们停止吗？

sentences.en: Or is that too much of a risk?
sentences.zh: 还是说风险太大了？

sentences.en: Are we taking the risk that we're going to lose our tax exemption, have to pay penalty taxes?
sentences.zh: 我们是否在冒着失去免税资格、必须缴纳惩罚性税款的风险？

sentences.en: Should we make some change in the meantime?
sentences.zh: 我们是否应该在此期间做出一些改变？

sentences.en: Are they making change in the meantime?
sentences.zh: 他们在此期间做出改变了吗？

sentences.en: As somebody who's talked to many, many of these groups, I will say no.
sentences.zh: 作为一个采访过许多这类组织的人，我会说没有。

sentences.en: Some of them have talked about making changes.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人谈到了做出改变。

sentences.en: The only groups we've found making a change are the ones that had not actually gotten the IRS approval before the IRS changed its mind.
sentences.zh: 我们发现唯一做出改变的组织是那些在国税局改变主意之前还没有真正获得国税局批准的组织。

sentences.en: So there's one in the University of Michigan that was still in the queue for approval when the IRS changed its mind.
sentences.zh: 所以密歇根大学有一个集体在国税局改变主意时还在排队等待批准。

sentences.en: And they had to massively overhaul their operations to get approval.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不大规模重组业务以获得批准。

sentences.en: So where a lot of collectives pay 100% of their money to athletes, they had to change so they paid 70% of their money to other charities and only 30% of their money to athletes.
sentences.zh: 所以，在许多集体将100%的资金支付给运动员的地方，他们不得不改变，将70%的资金支付给其他慈善机构，只有30%的资金支付给运动员。

sentences.en: So imagine if you have to convert your collective to run on that model,
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下，如果你必须转换你的集体来按照那种模式运行，

sentences.en: 70% of your money doesn't go to the athletes.
sentences.zh: 70%的资金不会流向运动员。

sentences.en: You know, try telling that to your donors.
sentences.zh: 你知道，试着告诉你的捐赠者这一点。

sentences.en: And how much more money would you have to raise to have the same impact on your school?
sentences.zh: 为了对你的学校产生同样的影响，你还需要筹集多少钱？

sentences.en: It certainly seems as though this system is flawed, and it's drawing increasing criticism.
sentences.zh: 这个系统看起来确实是有缺陷的，并且正招致越来越多的批评。

sentences.en: There are questions about the legality of it.
sentences.zh: 关于其合法性存在一些质疑。

sentences.en: So how is the body that sets the rules for college sports, the NCAA, responding?
sentences.zh: 那么，制定大学体育规则的机构——NCAA，对此有何回应？

sentences.en: Well, so far, they've responded really weakly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，到目前为止，他们的回应非常软弱。

sentences.en: In fact, the only case we know of where anyone's been punished for NIL being used in recruiting, which again is against the rules, is a case where at the University of Miami,
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们所知的唯一一起因在招募中使用NIL（姓名、形象和肖像权）而受到惩罚的案例——再次强调，这违反了规则——发生在迈阿密大学。

sentences.en: a booster who was paying a lot of NIL money to players sort of took pictures of himself, live tweeted himself recruiting two players from another school to Miami.
sentences.zh: 一位向球员支付大量NIL资金的赞助人，在招募两名来自其他学校的球员到迈阿密时，甚至还拍了照片，并进行了现场直播。

sentences.en: In that case, where the proof was on the internet, the NCAA punished the Miami basketball team lightly.
sentences.zh: 在那起证据确凿的案例中，NCAA对迈阿密篮球队进行了轻微的处罚。

sentences.en: Nobody else that we know of has been punished in that way.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，没有其他人受到过类似的惩罚。

sentences.en: But the NCAA sees what's happening and I think realizes two things.
sentences.zh: 但NCAA看到了正在发生的事情，我认为他们意识到了两点。

sentences.en: One, that it's encouraged huge, wide-scale disobedience of its rules, and also that it's allowed a shift of power from the schools themselves
sentences.zh: 第一，这助长了对其规则的大规模、广泛的违抗；第二，这导致权力从学校本身转移到了……

sentences.en: to these donor-run collectives that the conferences, the schools and the NCAA are alarmed by.
sentences.zh: 这些由捐赠者运营的集体组织手中，而各大联盟、学校和NCAA都对此感到担忧。

sentences.en: So what they've done is propose a pretty significant overhaul of the way these rules work.
sentences.zh: 所以他们所做的，是提议对这些规则的运作方式进行相当重大的改革。

sentences.en: Okay, what is it?
sentences.zh: 好的，具体是什么？

sentences.en: At the core of it, the idea is that schools would now be able to pay their own players directly.
sentences.zh: 其核心理念是，学校现在可以直接向自己的球员支付报酬。

sentences.en: So the thing that collectives do now, paying the players through this NIL system, nominally paying them for their name, image, and likeness, but really just paying them to play,
sentences.zh: 所以，目前由集体组织通过NIL系统支付给球员的费用——名义上是支付他们的姓名、形象和肖像权，但实际上只是付钱让他们打球——

sentences.en: that function would now be shifted to the schools themselves.
sentences.zh: 这一职能现在将转移给学校本身。

sentences.en: So the school athletic department could pay one of its offensive linemen for his quote-unquote name, image, and likeness rights, and the collective wouldn't be necessary anymore.
sentences.zh: 这样，学校的体育部门就可以为一名进攻锋线球员支付所谓的“姓名、形象和肖像权”费用，而集体组织就不再是必需的了。

sentences.en: I think the floor would be $30,000 per player, and it could go up from there.
sentences.zh: 我认为每位球员的底薪会是3万美元，而且还会在此基础上增加。

sentences.en: How would that actually work in practice?
sentences.zh: 这在实践中到底该如何运作？

sentences.en: Because I have to imagine that not every school can afford to pay all of their athletes at least $30,000.
sentences.zh: 因为我不得不设想，并非每所学校都能负担得起向所有运动员支付至少3万美元的费用。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Now, obviously, this is just a proposal.
sentences.zh: 当然，这目前只是一个提议。

sentences.en: It's a long way from becoming a reality, but it's interesting to see how the NCAA imagines that if it did become reality, the world would change.
sentences.zh: 距离成为现实还有很长的路要走，但看看NCAA如何设想如果它真的成为现实，世界会发生怎样的变化，这很有趣。

sentences.en: And what it imagines is basically a league of super teaMs.
sentences.zh: 他们设想的基本上是一个超级球队联盟。

sentences.en: You're going to take the top 30 teams in college football, which are the ones that can afford to pay their players and be in this game, and you're going to cleave them off
sentences.zh: 你将挑选大学橄榄球界最顶尖的30支球队，也就是那些有能力支付球员薪水并参与这场游戏的球队，将他们剥离出来，

sentences.en: and make them into sort of like a miniature NFL.
sentences.zh: 把他们变成一个类似于迷你NFL（美国国家橄榄球联盟）的组织。

sentences.en: So that's bad for the people who are on the outside of that system looking in.
sentences.zh: 所以这对那些被排除在系统之外的人来说是件坏事。

sentences.en: You know, if you root for Washington State or Minnesota or Rice or Vanderbilt, one of these schools that probably isn't going to have the money to compete or want to compete,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你支持华盛顿州立大学、明尼苏达大学、莱斯大学或范德比尔特大学，这些可能没有财力竞争或不想竞争的学校，

sentences.en: at least now you have the sense that, like, maybe if everything goes right, you could be a Cinderella team.
sentences.zh: 至少现在你还会觉得，如果一切顺利，你或许能成为一匹黑马。

sentences.en: You know, there's still theoretically a chance for you to be in the national championship.
sentences.zh: 你知道，理论上你仍然有机会进入全国冠军赛。

sentences.en: Now, you know, Cinderella's at home with the mice.
sentences.zh: 现在，你知道，灰姑娘只能和老鼠待在家里了。

sentences.en: There's no chance.
sentences.zh: 根本没机会了。

sentences.en: You're, like, legally never going to compete for that championship, and you're playing for a second-class crown.
sentences.zh: 从法律上讲，你永远不可能去争夺那个冠军，你只能去争夺二流的头衔。

sentences.en: Maybe people are okay with that, but it changes what it means to be a fan of those schools.
sentences.zh: 也许人们对此无所谓，但这改变了作为这些学校球迷的意义。

sentences.en: And under this proposal, in this theoretical super league, are the universities treating their players, the students, like employees?
sentences.zh: 而且根据这个提议，在这个理论上的超级联盟中，大学会把球员——也就是学生——当作雇员来对待吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不会。

sentences.en: So the schools would take the function of paying the players from the collectives and take it for themselves, but they would still want to pursue this kind of, like, quirky logic
sentences.zh: 所以学校会从集体组织手中接管支付球员报酬的职能，但他们仍然想坚持这种古怪的逻辑，

sentences.en: to make sure that the students are not employees because the NCAA still doesn't want to take on the employer-employee relationship with students and all the other rights
sentences.zh: 以确保学生不是雇员，因为NCAA仍然不想与学生建立雇主与雇员的关系，也不想承担所有其他权利，

sentences.en: to collective bargaining, you know, employment law protections, workers' comp, all the things that would come with that relationship.
sentences.zh: 比如集体谈判、劳动法保护、工伤赔偿，以及所有随之而来的权利。

sentences.en: This is an effort to keep that out whilst taking the function of paying the players in.
sentences.zh: 这是一种在接管支付球员职能的同时，试图规避这些责任的努力。

sentences.en: Hearing this proposal, it seems like the NCAA is really walking this tightrope where it is proposing a change, but not fully embracing the idea that college athletes
sentences.zh: 听到这个提议，感觉NCAA真的在走钢丝，它提议进行改革，但并没有完全接受大学运动员

sentences.en: should be treated like professionals.
sentences.zh: 应该被视为职业球员的观点。

sentences.en: There's financial reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 这背后有经济原因。

sentences.en: You know, the schools want to keep as much of this huge amount of money for themselves and not share it with players, but there's also something that's really fundamental
sentences.zh: 你知道，学校想把这笔巨额资金尽可能多地留给自己，而不是与球员分享，但大学体育中还有一些非常根本的东西，

sentences.en: about college sports that I think they worry about being lost, and that is the magic of college sports is that it's not professional sports.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们担心会失去这些，那就是大学体育的魔力在于它不是职业体育。

sentences.en: You know, there's this idea that the players play for the fight song and the school spirit and the meaning of what it means to be a Texas Longhorn or, you know, A&M Aggie
sentences.zh: 你知道，有一种观念认为球员们是为了校歌、学校精神，以及作为德克萨斯长角牛队或农工大学农校生队的一员的意义而战，

sentences.en: or whoever else.
sentences.zh: 或者其他任何学校。

sentences.en: So when you cheer in the stands and they play in the field, you're all part of something that's bigger than just money.
sentences.zh: 所以当你在看台上欢呼，他们在场上比赛时，你们都是超越金钱的事物的一部分。

sentences.en: And if you make it money, if college sports becomes mercenaries going from place to place, you know, for salaries,
sentences.zh: 如果你把它变成金钱交易，如果大学体育变成了雇佣兵为了薪水从一个地方跳到另一个地方，

sentences.en: I think they're worried that they'll lose the thing that has made college sports such a zillion-dollar industry that it'll just become basically a minor league, and who cares about
sentences.zh: 我想他们担心会失去让大学体育成为价值万亿产业的东西，它最终会变成一个次级联赛，而谁会在乎

sentences.en: minor league sports?
sentences.zh: 次级联赛呢？

sentences.en: I have to ask, honestly, as a viewer of college sports,
sentences.zh: 我必须诚实地问，作为一名大学体育的观众，

sentences.en: was there any of that amateurism really left in football, for example?
sentences.zh: 比如在橄榄球中，还有多少业余精神残留？

sentences.en: I mean, so much of it already feels like a professional sport.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它已经感觉像是一项职业运动了。

sentences.en: The money that comes in, not to the players, but to the schools, the number of viewers, the stakes, I mean, I'd imagine college football already has more viewers
sentences.zh: 流入的资金——不是给球员的，而是给学校的——观众人数，赌注，我的意思是，我想大学橄榄球的观众人数已经超过了

sentences.en: than the NHL, for example.
sentences.zh: NHL（国家冰球联盟），例如。

sentences.en: I mean, in so many ways, this was already professionalized.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在很多方面，这已经职业化了。

sentences.en: The only thing that seemed different before was that the labor was free.
sentences.zh: 以前唯一看起来不同的地方是劳动力是免费的。

sentences.en: I think of this as sort of like a Santa Claus problem, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为这就像一个“圣诞老人问题”，对吧？

sentences.en: If you want to believe in Santa Claus, you go looking for reasons to believe that.
sentences.zh: 如果你想相信圣诞老人，你就会去寻找相信的理由。

sentences.en: And until you see the guy in the mall take off his beard and see that it's not Santa Claus, until you're forced to sort of see that the illusion is an illusion,
sentences.zh: 直到你看到商场里的人摘下胡子，发现那不是圣诞老人，直到你被迫看到幻觉终究是幻觉，

sentences.en: you know, you're looking for reasons to believe.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你一直在寻找相信的理由。

sentences.en: That's the case with football fans like me.
sentences.zh: 像我这样的橄榄球迷就是这样。

sentences.en: The illusion that's being perpetrated here that we want to believe in is that those guys in the field are doing it for me.
sentences.zh: 这里所制造的、我们想要相信的幻觉是，场上的那些家伙是为了我而战。

sentences.en: They're doing it because they love the school that I love.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做是因为他们热爱我所热爱的学校。

sentences.en: They're doing it because they believe in the fight song and the ethos and the lore of the school.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做是因为他们相信校歌、精神以及学校的传统。

sentences.en: They're out there playing hard because me in the stands and them on the field, we're all supporting the same institution.
sentences.zh: 他们在场上拼搏，因为我在看台上，他们在场上，我们都在支持同一个机构。

sentences.en: So what these collectives have done, and it's sort of ironic that they are such shadowy, secretive organizations, their existence and the way that they have sort of, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以这些集体组织所做的事情——讽刺的是，它们是如此阴暗、隐秘的组织——它们的存在以及它们以某种方式，你知道，

sentences.en: brought the payment of players, normalized it, brought it into the light, has sort of changed the illusions, made it impossible to see that that's,
sentences.zh: 让支付球员报酬的行为正常化，将其带到阳光下，这在某种程度上改变了幻觉，让人无法再相信，

sentences.en: to believe that's Santa Claus, right?
sentences.zh: 无法再相信那是圣诞老人了，对吧？

sentences.en: And I think that's going to change the way that the college sports goes on in the future.
sentences.zh: 我认为这会改变未来大学体育的发展方式。

sentences.en: It's certainly a benefit for players.
sentences.zh: 这对球员来说当然是有利的。

sentences.en: The question is, what does it mean for fans?
sentences.zh: 问题是，这对球迷意味着什么？

sentences.en: And, you know, if our illusion goes away, does that change the popularity of the sport?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果我们的幻觉消失了，这会改变这项运动的受欢迎程度吗？

sentences.en: Does it change what draws people in?
